This is a backend proposal (C) built pipeline-graph-first. It is design only; I changed no other project file. The one GPU unit of work stays the existing Job, with the same single queue and single gpu-worker thread. A job either has `plan = null` or a typed `JobPlan`. With `plan = null` it is today's image-to-3D path: `ImageTo3DPipeline.run` is called exactly as now, so `model.glb` and the stored `settings` stay byte-identical. Otherwise a new `PlanRunner` executes the steps in order: `source_image`, `source_job`, `text_to_image`, `preprocess`, `segmentation_2d`, `reconstruct` (which wraps the unchanged pipeline), `lift_labels`, `part_extraction`, `export`. `part_refine` and `tune` are reserved and locked.

All request forms compile through a server-side `PlanCompiler` into one canonical plan: legacy bodies, the simple form (`source` plus `settings.parts`) and the Node UI graph (`pipeline`, with node types, ports, params schemas and templates taken from `GET /pipeline/catalog`). A graph equal to "input image → image-to-3D → export" compiles to `plan = null`.

- **Job kinds:** `image_to_3d`, `prompt_to_3d` and `part_decomposition`. The last one is a derived re-run on a completed job; it copies the parent's artifacts and does not wait for TRELLIS.
- **Progress:** the `JobStage` list, the percent formula and the `/system` keys are untouched. Steps report under `preprocessing` before reconstruction and `finalizing` after it. Per-step status, the plan percent and the plan ETA live in `Job.plan`, delivered through the existing `job.updated` event.
- **Providers:** text-to-image, 2D segmentation, lifting, part extraction and future 3D segmenters, completers and part generators each have a spec with licence metadata. Their states are honest (`not_approved`, `missing_dependencies`, `not_installed`, `license_required`, `unsupported`, `available`, `ready`, `error`). A model provider is usable only after the user approves it (`IMG3D_PROVIDERS_APPROVED`). Weights are installed only through a CLI that requires `--accept-license`.
- **GPU sharing:** a `GpuResidencyManager` loads helper models lazily, offloads them after each step, and adds an optional `release_vram()` for TRELLIS.
- **Parts:** 2D masks are lifted onto the faces of `model.glb`. Face and body stay one surface with regions marked per face (`_PART_ID`). Eyes, hair, clothes, accessories and detachable objects become separate nodes in one GLB that shares the original texture, with seam loops so they reassemble exactly. Eyebrows and eyelashes are deferred (mask now, geometry later). A versioned manifest (`img3d.parts/1`) records parts and their relationships.
- **API additions:** `/features`, `/pipeline/catalog`, `/pipeline/validate`, `/providers` routes, part and step file routes, `POST /jobs/{id}/parts/rebuild`, a `?kind=` filter, the `features.updated` event and new error codes.
- **Tuning:** hidden behind `IMG3D_FEATURE_MESH_TUNING=false`. Refine nodes are locked, and a refinement-consumer registry refuses registration while `IMG3D_PART_REFINEMENT_ENABLED=false`. No tuning algorithms are added.

The document also says exactly what the frontend needs, gives a per-file test plan, and splits the work into 11 slices (S0–S10) with disjoint file ownership, dependencies, merge order and acceptance criteria.

It ends with 8 questions only you can decide:
1. Which text-to-image model to approve.
2. Which segmentation stack to approve.
3. Whether models install by CLI only or also from inside the app.
4. Whether to add `IMG3D_BLENDER_ENABLED=false` to your `.env` now.
5. Whether open surface patches are acceptable as separated parts for this milestone.
6. Whether to add an image-review step before 3D.
7. Whether a separate process for transformers-5 models is allowed.
8. How many multi-view lifting views to run by default.

I wrote the frontend proposal. It is a design only; no other project file was changed.

**Architecture**
- Four UI modes render over the existing `api/` and zustand stores. Shared commands go in a new `src/actions/` and derived logic in `src/hooks/`.
- Pure, Node-testable logic goes in `src/lib/`, `src/domain/` and `src/workflow/`.
- The Default UI stays in the first bundle and reuses today's `Header`, `AppShell` and `HistoryDrawer` from their current paths, with no file moves. Node, Mobile and Tablet load lazily.
- Each feature panel is split into a body component and a card wrapper with the same name and path, so Default looks the same while sheets, the tablet side panel and the node inspector reuse the bodies.
- A new preferences store saves the UI mode in `img3d.preferences` (default `'default'`). An "App settings" dialog switches modes and survives the switch; `?ui=` gives a temporary override that is not saved.
- Feature code no longer switches the Default mobile tab directly. It asks a new navigation store to show a view, and each shell maps that request.

**Image-to-3D stays unchanged**
- Every mode, including Node, builds jobs through one function. A test checks that the request is identical to today's when the input is an image and parts are off.
- On a backend without the new features endpoint, Default shows exactly today's UI plus one App settings gear.

**Node UI**
- Six nodes: Input Image, Prompt, Segmentation, Image-to-3D, Part Extraction, Export.
- A locked "Refinement" group reserves the slot for future tuning nodes.
- The graph stores only topology, node modes and layout; all settings stay in the shared stores, so Default and Node always show the same values.
- Connections are validated, and per-node status comes from the job's progress and step updates.
- It uses `@xyflow/react` 12.12.0 (MIT), loaded only in Node mode. A list view gives keyboard and touch use without dragging.

**Mobile and Tablet**
- Mobile: full-screen viewer, floating bottom bar with a Generate button, and slide-up sheets for create, parts, library and progress.
- Tablet switches automatically: left side rail in landscape at 840 px or wider, bottom bar otherwise, and the phone layout below 600 px. It does not flip while the keyboard is open.

**Parts in the viewer:** an assembled parts model loads as a third model. Separate parts are shown or hidden directly; regions on the continuous body are hidden or highlighted on the GPU. Clicking a part selects it in the list, and toggles never reload the model.

**Backend assumptions to reconcile:** a features endpoint with an honest model registry, an optional prompt `source` and `settings.parts` on job creation, optional `kind`/`source`/`steps` on jobs, part-analysis runs plus a manifest, and two new WebSocket events. One adapter handles parts either as a separate run (recommended) or inside the job.

**Tuning:** the tuner UI shows only if both a build flag and the backend allow it; `components/meshTuner/*` is not touched.

**Also included:** a Default polish list (P1–P20) for verified breakages, accessibility checklist, size budget (first-load JS ≤195 kB gzip), quality gates, test plan, and five waves of slices with separate file ownership.

**Before slice A1:** commit or stash the uncommitted tuner edits in four frontend files, since A1 edits `api/types.ts`.

Open questions are in §21: parts shape, one-step vs two-step prompt flow, model approvals, adding `@xyflow/react`, the "App settings" name, segmentation preview, contrast changes, a device hint, and workflow file import/export.

Wrote the risk-first backend proposal A (about 1,000 lines, no TBD placeholders). The working image-to-3D job is left completely untouched. All part-aware work happens in follow-up runs that read a finished job, plus one orchestrator that chains existing public service calls. It follows the user's DECISIONS.md (found in the part-aware folder during this task): Z-Image-Turbo for prompts, the five chosen segmentation models, eye areas cut as separate meshes, eyebrows and eyelashes kept as records with geometry deferred.

How it stays safe:
- Generation, progress, model, schema, job-service and storage files are frozen. A new test pins their sha256 hashes, so model.glb, job.json, JobOut, the JobStage list, the percent formula and the /system keys cannot change by accident.
- Only four small seams touch working code: a ~12-line GenerationWorker.submit_gpu_task that reuses the single gpu-worker thread; an optional ServiceContainer.part_aware field plus lifecycle start/stop (stopped before the generation worker); router, event-type and create_app(part_providers=) additions; and new optional Settings fields.

New resources, built on one generic run framework copied from the tuner pattern:
- ig_: prompt to candidate images. "Use candidate" goes through the existing upload_image, so prompt-to-3D needs no change to CreateJobRequest.
- sg_: 2D segmentation before reconstruction (on a reference image) or after (on a finished job). The crop TRELLIS used is recovered without touching the TRELLIS code (recomputed from alpha or template-matched).
- pa_: after reconstruction. Three strategies: components (CPU, no ML, works today), semantic_regions and semantic_parts. Outputs a manifest (img3d.parts/1), an assembled multi-node GLB sharing one texture set, face labels and seam loops, and checks that the parts reassemble exactly.
- wf_: server-side chain prompt → image → segmentation → existing job → parts → export. This is what the Node UI's Run calls.

Other contents:
- GET /features and GET /models with honest model states, licence data, the node catalog and the taxonomy. The shape is compatible with the frontend proposal B adapter.
- Full endpoint table with status codes, five new WebSocket events, new error classes, storage layout and retention, and every feature flag.
- Tuning gates: IMG3D_BLENDER_ENABLED=false in .env as the hard gate, /features reporting it off, an import-boundary test, and a locked part-consumer registry with no implementations.
- Test plan; all 182 existing tests stay unmodified.
- 13 slices with separate file ownership and acceptance criteria. Phase A runs in order (contract and guards, then skeleton and frozen interfaces), then the parallel slices, then part analysis, workflows and the frontend API slice.

Six items are deferred until the user approves them, including saving TRELLIS intermediate data, per-part regeneration, a per-part texture atlas and tuning consumers. Six open questions remain:
1. Vendoring See-through and Sapiens2 as git submodules.
2. Whether prompt jobs pick the first candidate automatically or wait for the user.
3. Whether to also block the tuner in code, which means editing an existing test file.
4. Whether the eye cut should include an eyelid ring.
5. Whether to export per-part GLBs and a zip by default.
6. When to approve saving the TRELLIS intermediates.

I wrote the frontend proposal B (command layer plus workflow engine) to the file above. It is about 2,170 lines. No other project file was changed; other agents' design files share that folder.

**Workflow document.** One document, saved in the browser as `img3d.workflow`, describes every generation in all four UI modes. It holds the graph of the six nodes (Input Image, Prompt, Segmentation, Image-to-3D, Part Extraction, Export), their values and the node-editor layout. Generation settings and reference images stay in their existing stores, linked rather than copied, so nothing that works today moves.

**Engine.** It is plain TypeScript (no React, axios or React Flow), so the tests run under Node 22's type stripping. It covers the node registry, typed ports, validation with exact messages, and building the backend request. With the default template (image input, parts off) it produces exactly today's job request, byte for byte; a golden test pins this. Node status comes from the optional new `job.steps`, or from the existing stages for old jobs.

**Command layer.** About 60 commands with fixed ids and exact payloads are the only way the UI changes state. Each decides availability from one shared state snapshot. That single check drives the disabled reasons, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, the Node Run button, the mobile Generate button and the tablet rail. The existing "can generate" reasons keep their wording.

**The four modes.**
- **Default** keeps today's layout and adds an Image | Prompt switch, a parts card and a settings gear. The 17-item polish list includes the breakages already measured at 320 px, 812×375 and 768×1024.
- **Mobile** has a floating bottom nav, a Generate button and bottom sheets.
- **Tablet** switches automatically: a left rail in landscape, a bottom nav in portrait or narrow windows.
- **Node** uses React Flow behind a small wrapper and has a keyboard-friendly list view.

The chosen mode is saved as `img3d.preferences`, default "default", with a `?ui=` override for testing.

**Parts.** A manifest parser accepts both manifest drafts in the research. The single existing viewer gains show/hide, isolate, highlight and an exploded view. Body regions can be highlighted only if the backend includes a `_PART_ID` attribute; otherwise the UI says so.

**Tuning stays hidden.** It shows only if a build flag (off by default) and the backend's `mesh_tuning.enabled` are both on, so a default build sends no `/blender` or `/tunings` requests. Future tuning nodes have a locked registry slot with no nodes in it.

**Backend shapes assumed** (all additive, listed exactly with a reconciliation table):
- `GET /features`, with installed and licence states for models;
- optional `source` and `settings.parts` on job creation, sent only for keys the backend advertises;
- optional `kind`, `source` and `steps` on jobs, and `parts` on results;
- part file routes and an optional rebuild endpoint.

If the backend returns 404 for `/features`, the app falls back to image-only and says why.

**Also in the file:** stores and saved keys, state machines, accessibility checklist, performance budget, test plan, quality-gate commands, and 13 slices in four waves with separate files per agent and acceptance criteria. The only new package is `@xyflow/react` 12.12.0, loaded only in Node mode.

**Ten open questions** are listed. The main ones: where the features endpoint lives, which optional request fields the backend accepts, your model choices and whether the app gets an Install button, a review step for prompt jobs, one shared workflow for all modes, and adding Playwright.

This proposal designs the part-aware asset data model first and derives the pipeline, API, storage and tests from it. It is about 2,060 lines and is design only: no project file other than this one was changed.

**Asset model.** A completed job is one unchanging asset revision: the untouched `model.glb` plus an optional `parts/` folder described by a versioned manifest (`img3d.parts/1`). The manifest is fully specified with a worked example. Every per-face array refers to the faces of `model.glb`, so all revisions share one face numbering. Semantic labels (`face_labels`) are stored separately from which mesh owns each face (`face_owner`), so semantic regions never cut the mesh.

**Part kinds.** Four kinds: `host` (the continuous body), `physical`, `physical_deferred` and `region`.
- Physical: eyes, hair, clothes, accessories and detachable objects.
- Physical-deferred: eyebrows and eyelashes. TRELLIS only paints them, so they ship now as a mask plus a 3D region plus guide curves; real geometry comes later.
- Region: face and body areas.

**Splitting is reversible.** Cuts weld duplicate vertices and record ordered boundary loops (seams) and per-mesh vertex maps. Reassembling the parts reproduces the base mesh bit-exactly; this is a tested invariant. All parts share one texture atlas, and there is no re-bake. The manifest also covers the part graph, coordinate frames, cameras, provenance (models, licences, revision lineage) and a per-part `refinement` block that is locked.

**Pipeline.** One GPU queue and worker, as today. Jobs get a `kind`: `image_to_3d`, `prompt_to_3d` or `part_decomposition`. Re-decomposing an existing asset creates a new job that hard-links the parent's files. A router sends legacy requests to the unchanged `ImageTo3DPipeline.run`, and the worker file is not edited. No new stages: an optional `Job.pipeline` lists the steps (`prompt`, `input_image`, `segmentation`, `image_to_3d`, `part_extraction`, `export`) with its own percent. 2D segmentation runs on the exact conditioning image through a new optional engine method, and tests must show its pixels equal upstream's. With no segmentation model, a geometry-only mode (separate pieces) still produces real output.

**Model choices stay open.** Text-to-image, segmentation and mesh labelling sit behind pluggable providers and a model registry with licence data. They report honest states such as not approved, missing dependency or not installed, and a matrix shows what each approved subset of models gives you.

**API.** All additions are optional: `/features` (flags, provider states, request keys, the node catalogue), `/taxonomy`, `/models`, part file routes, a whitelisted job-file route, and `/jobs/{id}/parts/rebuild`. Two new error codes (`capability_unavailable`, `feature_disabled`) and two new WebSocket events (`features.updated`, `model.updated`). `/system` and the progress formula are unchanged.

**Tuning gate.** New setting `tuning_enabled=false` makes creating a tuning run return 503. The tuner tests need a one-line opt-in. The refinement plug-in registry refuses every registration.

**Also included:** what the frontend needs from the API (with a name reconciliation against `frontend_b_command_engine.md`), a backward-compatibility matrix, a test plan by file and assertion, and 15 implementation slices (S0–S14) in waves with disjoint file ownership and acceptance criteria. Model-dependent slices (S8, S13, S14) wait for your approval.

**Open questions:** 10 for you, including which text-to-image and segmentation models, whether the app may download models, the server-side tuning gate, eyebrow/eyelash deferral, per-part files, rebuilds shown in history, and default view counts.

strengths: Smallest workable seam over the code that already works. DefaultShell is eager and imports today's Header, AppShell and HistoryDrawer from their current paths with no file moves. uiStore (mobileTab, historyOpen) is left unchanged. Feature panels keep their names and paths, and each XxxPanel is just Panel + XxxContent, so Default renders the same DOM, checked by a ui_probe fingerprint.

Legacy backend safety is explicit. On a 404 from /features, Default hides the prompt and parts UI and stays pixel-identical apart from the App settings gear. Every new request field is sent only when advertised and enabled, and parts:null or enabled:false is never sent.

There is one pure request builder, lib/jobRequest.buildCreateJobRequest, used by every mode including Node. Its byte- and key-order-identical test against jobStore.ts:L208-212 covers 6 form fixtures. toRequestSettings moves verbatim into a pure lib file and is re-exported, so existing imports still compile.

The Node graph is only a projection. It stores topology, mode and layout, never parameter values. deriveConfig writes through to the shared inputStore and partOptionsStore. pipelineBlock is set only while the Node shell is mounted and cleared on unmount, so a broken graph can never block Default, Mobile or Tablet generation.

It correctly spots the real chunking hazard: the vendor regex at vite.config.ts:L77 (priority 40) would capture the nested zustand@4 from @xyflow/react. It fixes this by anchoring the regex to the top-level node_modules and adding a budget check for what lands in the initial chunk.

Tuner gate needs two keys (build flag VITE_FEATURE_MESH_TUNER and features.tuning.mesh_tuner.state). It covers all choke points without touching components/meshTuner/*. There are no model install buttons; models are read-only with honest states and licence badges.

Slices are clear (A1-A4, B1-B2, C1-C4, D1-D4, E1) with disjoint ownership per wave and concrete acceptance criteria. Tests need no new tools: node --experimental-strip-types on Node 22.17, which is verified, plus import_boundaries.mjs and bundle_budget.mjs.
weaknesses: Highlighting parts in the viewer uses a 256x1 DataTexture plus an onBeforeCompile shader patch (discard, dither, emissive) chained into the clay, normals and wireframe view materials. This is the riskiest code in the proposal, and it depends on GLTFLoader's handling of _FEATURE_ID_0, which is unverified.
It hedges between two backend shapes ('runs' and 'job') with a synthesising adapter in api/parts.ts. That is extra code and more test surface, when one variant should simply be chosen.

Its PartOptionsIn puts fine taxonomy ids in `separate` (clothing.outer, object.held) and has no `regions` key. backend_contract_map L357-362 specifies group ids (eyes, eyebrows, eyelashes, hair, clothes, accessories, detachable) plus `regions`. This must be reconciled, or an extra='forbid' backend will return 422 for parts-enabled requests.

The Node engine's semantic output is a 3-boolean PipelineConfig. Future tuning or refine nodes will need PipelineConfig, the stores and deriveConfig extended. There is no per-node param schema or contribute() hook, so it is less extensible than B.
Its prerequisite is stale. It says four tuner files have uncommitted edits, but git status shows a clean frontend tree at commit 8654b90.
It adds many new stores (preferences, navigation, features, input, partOptions, part, workflow) and new folders (actions/, domain/, shells/shared). That is still sizeable, but each one is additive.

strengths: The workflow engine is very strong and extensible: ParamDef schemas, a contribute() and compile() pipeline with a fixed key order, a locked 'refine' category the registry enforces (it throws on an unlocked refine def), templates, a docFromJob mapping, and serialize/migrate. This is the best base for future tuning nodes.

Golden request tests G1-G5 cover G1 parity with primary_image_id null, advanced overrides and a legacy FeatureSet. The plan also checks in the browser pane that the POST body equals G1 in all four modes.

request_keys gating per capability means the frontend sends an optional key (subject, segmenter_id, model_id, preset, style, ...) only when the backend advertises it. This is the right defence against extra='forbid'.

PartOptionsIn matches backend_contract_map §4.3: user-facing group ids plus `regions`, with a PartGroupInfo that carries default_kind, default_selected and a note such as the eyelash 'geometry deferred' note.
The test double is good: mock --strict-requests mirrors extra='forbid', and the test-only request log at /api/__test/requests turns 'zero /blender or /tunings requests' into an automated assertion.

The viewer plan is simpler: object.visible for physical parts, an overlay mesh plus a cached index subset for regions, and an honest 'Highlight unavailable' when the attribute is missing. There is no shader patching.
There is an exact table mapping legacy job stages to node status, plus a session runIndex StepMap so nodes re-created after Run show idle. Mobile landscape switches to a rail with side sheets.
weaknesses: It brings in many new concepts under the simplicity lens: a command bus, CommandSpec factories plus binds, a vanilla AppSnapshot kept in sync by state/sync syncers (a second copy of store state; its R3 risk is snapshot lag), state/read and state/reactions, pending, announcer and transfer stores, import.meta.glob self-registration (its R2 risk is silent misses), a linear renderer with placement maps, and a panel registry.

It rewrites a lot of working code. AppShell, Header and MobileTabBar move into renderers/default behind shims. S6 migrates every component in references, settings, generation and history off direct store access. mobileTab and historyOpen move out of uiStore. App.tsx is replaced by AppRoot. The user explicitly asked for incremental work and reuse.

The Default image-to-3D path now compiles from a persisted workflow doc shared across modes. A Node-UI edit, such as deleting Image-to-3D, blocks Generate in Default until 'Restore default workflow'. G1 parity is proven only for the canonical doc.

Its chunking mitigation is wrong. It sets the xyflow group at priority 35 and claims that outranks vendor (R5), but vendor is priority 40 with an unanchored regex (vite.config.ts:L77), so the nested zustand@4 would land in the initial chunk.

It goes beyond scope with a model-install endpoint (E10), a LicenseDialog, an install state machine and models.updated. This presumes decisions the user has not made yet, and no backend design defines it.

Ownership is harder to follow. S3 creates a temporary renderers/default entry that S7 later takes over. S2 depends on S1's bridge. S6 owns very large directory sets, and the per-slice allowlist files must shrink.

fatal_flaws: No strictly fatal flaw was found in A (frontend_a_shells). It must still change one thing before slice A1 merges: its PartOptionsIn (taxonomy ids in `separate`, no `regions`) differs from backend_contract_map L357-362. Against an extra='forbid' backend that would return 422 on parts-enabled requests; the image path is unaffected because parts are omitted when off. Its prerequisite about uncommitted tuner files is also stale: git status shows a clean frontend tree at commit 8654b90.

B (frontend_b_command_engine), a must-fix build defect: its plan puts the xyflow chunk group at priority 35 and claims that outranks vendor. But the existing vendor group is priority 40 with the unanchored regex /node_modules[\\/](zustand|use-sync-external-store)[\\/]/ (vite.config.ts:L77). B, a high risk to the working pipeline: Default generation is recompiled from a persisted workflow doc shared across modes (img3d.workflow). A Node-UI edit, such as deleting Image-to-3D, or a migrated doc changes or blocks Generate in the Default UI. G1 parity is proven only for the canonical doc. Together with migrating every working component off direct store access (S6) and moving AppShell, Header and MobileTabBar into renderers/default (S7), this is the large rewrite of working code the user asked to avoid.

B, out of scope for the milestone: model install from the UI (E10 POST /models/{id}/install, the LicenseDialog, the models.install command, the install state machine and models.updated) lets the app start multi-GB weight downloads. It runs ahead of the user's pending model decision, and no backend design specifies it. Cut it, and keep models read-only with honest states as A does.

strengths: Changes the least of the working UI. DefaultShell imports today's Header, AppShell and HistoryDrawer from their current paths with no file moves, and uiStore stays unchanged, so the paused BlenderSetupDialog's setMobileTab still works. On a legacy backend (/features returns 404) Default stays the same as today apart from the App settings gear, and a ui_probe fingerprint test checks this.

Image-to-3D generation never depends on the node graph. Default, Mobile and Tablet build the request from stores through the pure buildCreateJobRequest(), and job_request.test.mjs checks that the image source with parts off is deep- and key-order-equal to the request jobStore.ts:L208-212 builds today. The Node shell only projects the graph onto the stores, and its pipelineBlock is cleared on unmount, so an invalid graph can never block the other modes.

Follows the research recommendation that node parameter values are not stored in the graph (frontend_architecture_map §5.6). Each node binds to an existing store, and reconcile() runs on Node mount, so Default and Node always edit the same form with no duplicated logic.

Shows part relationships well. PartInspector lists the parent, what the part is attached to or held by, its side, symmetric pairs and relations, and the outliner has hierarchy and category groupings. Refinement status is shown read-only as 'Eligible · untouched — refinement is paused'.

Segmentation can run before reconstruction (sg_ on a reference image) and after it (job conditioning image). Part analysis (pa_) follows reconstruction. The CPU 'components' strategy proves the manifest, GLB, routes and UI contract with real data and no ML.

The future-consumer interface is thin: PartConsumer has only plan(), there is no reader API, and partition uses glb.submesh, so vertex order is implicit. Per-part GLBs are off by default.

It default-approves the six DECISIONS.md models (default_approved=True), although the task frames model choice as pending. It also uses 15 GB VRAM for Z-Image-Turbo where the DECISIONS.md probe measured a 23.3 GB peak.

The manifest has explicit frames (asset, trellis, conditioning), the registered view camera, buffers with dtype, count and sha256, provenance and lineage.

Segmentation before reconstruction uses the exact conditioning pixels. The optional prepare_conditioning path is proven by an np.array_equal test against upstream preprocess_image, and test_generation_parity.py stays unchanged. Persisting latents is optional and consumes no RNG.

Job remains the single unit of GPU work and the UI gets one job.updated stream. The PipelineRouter sends legacy jobs to ImageTo3DPipeline.run unchanged. Job.pipeline has its own percent while the 9 frozen stages stay intact.

Failure semantics are explicit: a part-step failure leaves the job completed with parts.status=failed. Rebuilds are derived jobs (revision n+1, hard-linked base files). A §14.6 table shows what each approved model subset yields.
